title: Hiding at Val Verde from the MGM music head
summary: Lee and Jimmy Blanton hid in Val Verde while MGM sent a limousine to find him because only he could teach Mickey the solos.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: this is 2 or 3 weeks before they got to this part. I got no call. But I found out that they were getting ready to start shooting this part, and I knew that no one could teach him what I had played but me, because but maybe they couldn't teach him what they had played, you know?

So I left. Jimmy Blanton and I were very, very dear friends, and we went up to a place called Val Verdi, you know, and I told my mother that -- and my sister -- that if MGM tried to get me, don't tell them where I was, because I ...

It was a resort, yes. And so we went up to Val Verdi and sure enough, now they were in trouble -- because they had these drum solos down there, and they didn't have anyone to show Mickey what was done. Okay, so this big black limo that they use in studios -- I'm sure you've seen them, you know -- here's a chauffeur and the Head of the music department out there looking for me. So Blanton and I saw him, you know, because you're really crazy when you're young, you know, and he said, 'Hey, there he is!' And so I'm running and I'm hiding, and the guy is trying to find me, and so he finally finds me and he says, 'Look, you know, you're making me lose my job. I'm supposed to have you under contract.' And I said, 'I don't want to talk to you because you lied to me. You paid me $66 and I was supposed to get $500.' He said, 'Well, look, you got to come in because no one can do it.' And I said, 'I know no one can
do it, but I got to be paid for it."

And I wouldn't talk with him; I wouldn't deal with him at all. And he made me promise would I come to the studio with George Estelle and Louis B. Mayer and Mickey Rooney, and that's who I had an audience with.
